message.text:
The frontend auth interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts` as `authInterceptor`. A backend `Connect AuthInterceptor` also exists.

The interceptor manages two token kinds: a Bearer access token sent in the Authorization header, and a refresh token stored as a cookie with credentials enabled, consumed via a RefreshToken RPC. I am checking `connect.ts` and `auth-state` to confirm the exact refresh token storage mechanism.

The frontend interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts`. It manages access tokens (Bearer in Authorization header, stored in localStorage via `auth-state.ts`) and refresh tokens (HTTP-only cookie, sent with credentials). The backend package that validates these tokens is still being identified.

The backend package that validates tokens is `server/auth` (Authenticator). The frontend interceptor does not manage PATs; those are for programmatic access.

q29.
web/src/connect.ts; access token (JWT Bearer) and refresh token (cookie); server/auth

`authInterceptor` in `web/src/connect.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` from `web/src/auth-state.ts` and, on 401 or expiry, calls `AuthService.RefreshToken` with `credentials: "include"` so the refresh-token cookie is sent. The backend validates those tokens in `server/auth` (`Authenticator` in `authenticator.go`; JWT helpers in `token.go`).
